findings.area: Concurrency — non-atomic multi-file write vs live SSR read
findings.location: scrapers/run.py:98-116 (3× Path.write_text); web/src/lib/real-store.ts:28-53 (readJson + mtime-sum cache across the 3 files)
findings.issue: The scraper overwrites bestsellers.json, products.json, meta.json (and trends.py writes keywords.json) non-atomically while the request-time SSR app reads them, allowing a torn/partial read → JSON.parse throw, or a mutually-inconsistent set of files.
findings.evidence: Path.write_text is a truncate-then-write, not atomic (no os.replace/tempfile — `grep os.replace|tempfile scrapers` = none). real-store caches keyed on the SUM of all three mtimes, so a half-finished run busts the cache and re-reads a torn set. Already observable on disk from concurrent runs: meta.json product_count=135 & categories include 'books' while bestsellers.json all=120 (different runs/partial state).
findings.impact: Intermittent 500s on every page during the ~scrape window (twice daily), or silently inconsistent KPIs (counts/categories that disagree). readJson catches parse errors and returns null → for bestsellers that means available()=false → whole app flips to seed mid-request.
findings.fix: Make writes atomic: write to a .tmp then os.replace() (atomic on POSIX) for each file; ideally write all four to a temp dir and swap a single 'current' symlink/dir so readers always see a consistent set. On the read side, treat a parse failure as 'serve last-known-good', not 'fall back to seed'.

findings.area: Error/resilience boundaries — none exist
findings.location: web/src/app/** (no error.tsx / not-found.tsx / loading.tsx / global-error.tsx authored; find returned none)
findings.issue: There are no App-Router error or not-found boundaries, so any server exception (e.g. torn JSON read, unexpected null) renders Next's default blank error screen with no recovery, and notFound() for a bad ASIN shows the unstyled default 404.
findings.evidence: `find web/src/app -name error.tsx -o -name not-found.tsx -o -name loading.tsx -o -name global-error.tsx` → empty. products/[asin]/page.tsx:97 calls notFound() but no not-found.tsx exists. Build emitted only the framework defaults (_not-found.html, _global-error.html).
findings.impact: Poor failure UX and no isolation: a single page's data error can blank the route; the dynamic [asin] route accepts arbitrary input and 404s into an unbranded default page.
findings.fix: Add app/(app)/error.tsx (client boundary with reset), app/(app)/not-found.tsx, and a root app/global-error.tsx; optionally loading.tsx for the dynamic routes. Keep boundaries data-aware so a stale/missing-data state degrades gracefully rather than throwing.

findings.area: Stale static pages — build-time fs freeze
findings.issue: /watchlists and /alerts are statically prerendered and read product data via fs at BUILD time, so they bake in whatever data existed when the build ran and never reflect later scrapes (and on Vercel will bake the seed fallback per the Critical finding).
findings.evidence: prerender-manifest lists /alerts, /settings, /watchlists; watchlists.html/alerts.html exist in .next/server/app. getWatchlist maps fixed ASINs through getProduct() which hits real.available(). No export const dynamic/revalidate anywhere (`grep` = NONE).
findings.impact: Watchlist/alerts product fields (price/title) are frozen to build time; combined with the fs-tracing bug they will show seed values permanently in production.
findings.fix: Force these routes dynamic (export const dynamic='force-dynamic' or read at request time) once the data source is request-safe, or move user-owned data to Supabase as the schema already anticipates.

findings.area: Silent source failure — keywords/trends

findings.evidence: keywords.json on disk = {"keywords":[]}. real.keywords() returns null when empty → data.ts getKeywords falls through to seed KEYWORDS. trends.py autocomplete/pytrends failures are caught and the worker keeps the existing (empty) file; no health metric is surfaced to the UI.
findings.impact: A 'real data' platform shows fabricated demand keywords under real-source labeling; failure is invisible until someone inspects files.
findings.fix: Surface source health (e.g. a freshness/empty badge from meta.json + a per-source status), and have the UI explicitly label the demand panel as seed/sample when real.keywords() is null rather than seamlessly substituting.

dimensions.dimension: Frontend Correctness / A11y / UX-States (real amazon.eg data)
dimensions.summary: I audited every screen under web/src/app/(app)/** and the shared components against the REAL data the scraper writes (web/src/data/real/*.json: 120 bestseller rows, only 8 enriched with bsr/reviews_list, single-snapshot history, keywords present). The disclosure/empty-state discipline is genuinely strong on most screens (movers, reviews, keywords, search, products all have real empty states with honest copy, and confidence/provenance labels are pervasive). However there is one CRITICAL runtime crash and several correctness/consistency defects that surface specifically because real data replaced the seed. The Watchlists route crashes outright on real data because getWatchlist() hardcodes seed ASINs that do not exist in amazon.eg data and force-unwraps an undefined product. Separately, every product-detail page mislabels demand as "Unknown" and velocity as "Holding steady" because it re-derives those from the always-empty real movers list instead of the row's own band, while the same product shows a real band on the lists. The 112 non-enriched products render a blank 300px history chart and empty sparkline with no "not enough history yet" message. The locale toggle flips direction to RTL without translating any chrome, producing a broken mixed-direction layout. I empirically SSR-probed Recharts 3.8.0 to confirm empty/1-point charts do NOT throw (so they are a UX-quality issue, not a crash). Verdict: no-go until the Watchlists crash and the detail-page demand/velocity inconsistency are fixed.

findings.area: Watchlists screen — runtime crash on real data
findings.issue: getWatchlist() hardcodes seed ASINs ["B0EG0XIAM2","B0EG0PHIL6","B0EG0LORE9"] and builds items with `product: getProduct(asin)!`. In real mode getProduct delegates to real.product(asin), which searches bestsellers.all and products.json and returns undefined for these ASINs (they are seed-only; real ASINs are B0CPC8JMCW, B092312R94, …). The non-null assertion `!` masks the undefined, so WatchCard receives item.product === undefined and dereferences `const p = item.product; … p.titleEn` → throws.
findings.evidence: Verified the three seed ASINs are absent from BOTH bestsellers.json `all` (120 rows) and products.json `products` (8 keys): script output `B0EG0XIAM2: in_all=False in_products=False` (etc.). They DO exist in seed.ts:55,59,62. real-store.ts product() (lines 141-157) returns undefined when the ASIN is in neither file. watch-card.tsx line 37 `const p = item.product;` then line 50 `{p.titleEn}` with no guard (the only guard is `if (removed) return null`).
findings.impact: The entire /watchlists route throws on first render with the real dataset — a hard crash (Next.js error boundary / 500), not a graceful empty state. This is the default state for any user opening Watchlists, since the three items are seeded as 'tracked'.
findings.fix: Either (a) make getWatchlist() filter to products that resolve: `.map(asin => { const product = getProduct(asin); return product ? { asin, addedAt, product } : null }).filter(Boolean)`, or (b) seed the watchlist from real ASINs (e.g. getBestSellers({limit:3}).map(r => r.product.asin)) so it tracks products that actually exist. Also make WatchCard defensively render an empty/placeholder card if product is missing. Remove the `!` non-null assertion so the type system surfaces the gap.

findings.area: Product detail — demand band & rank velocity contradict the list screens
findings.issue: The detail page derives demandBand/riseScore/gainPct from `getMovers({period}).find(...)`. In real mode real.movers() ALWAYS returns [] (real-store.ts:137-139, by design — no velocity on day 1), so moverRow is always undefined → demandBand defaults to "unknown", riseScore=0, gainPct=0 for EVERY product. The header DemandBadge (line 194) and the 'Relative demand' KPI (line 240) therefore show "Unknown", and 'Rank velocity' shows +0% / "Holding steady" — even though the very same product on the dashboard/bestsellers list shows a real within-category band (e.g. "Very High") computed by real.bestSellers → bandFromPos.
findings.evidence: real-store.ts:137-139 `export function movers(){ return []; }`. Detail page line 107 `const demandBand = moverRow?.demandBand ?? "unknown";` ignores the product's own ranking row. Cross-checked: bestSellers() assigns demandBand via bandFromPos (real-store.ts:117-126), so list and detail disagree for all 120 products.
findings.impact: Same product shows two different, contradicting demand labels depending on the screen — a data-trust/consistency defect on the platform's core research surface. Users see a product ranked #1 'Very High' on the list, then 'Unknown / Holding steady' on its own page.
findings.fix: On the detail page, source demandBand from the product's bestseller row (e.g. getBestSellers({categoryNode: product.categoryNode}).find(r=>r.product.asin===asin)?.demandBand) rather than from movers. Show velocity as an explicit 'Not enough history yet' state when movers is empty, instead of a fabricated '+0% / Holding steady'.

findings.area: Product detail — blank history chart for the 112 non-enriched products (no empty state)
findings.issue: history.points is empty for the 112 of 120 products that are not in products.json (real.bsrHistory returns points:[] when leafBsr is null), and is exactly 1 point for the 8 enriched products (single snapshot). The page unconditionally renders <HistoryChart data={points}/> with no length guard, under a heading 'Rank & price history (90 days)' and a 'Relative'/medium confidence badge.
findings.evidence: Verified 112 non-enriched ASINs (meta.json enriched:8, product_count:120). real-store.ts bsrHistory (167-177) returns points:[] when leaf is null, else a single {date,value}. products.json bsr entries are {rank,category} with NO date, so even enriched products yield 1 point. I SSR-probed Recharts 3.8.0 with empty and 1-point data: both render WITHOUT throwing (123/127-char SVG), confirming this is a blank-frame UX issue, not a crash. A 1-point line draws no visible line (only an active dot on hover).
findings.impact: 112 product pages show an empty 300px chart titled '90 days' with no line and no explanation; 8 show an essentially blank chart. Misleading for a screen labelled with a confidence badge. Not a crash.
findings.fix: Guard: if points.length < 2, render an empty-state ('History starts building from your first daily snapshot — not enough data points yet') instead of the chart, matching the honest empty states already used for reviews/movers. The CardDescription already hints at this; surface it as the actual chart state.

findings.area: Ranking rows / sparkline — empty or single-point Spark for real rows
findings.issue: RankRow calls getBsrHistory(p.asin) for every row and feeds .points.map(pt=>pt.value) to <Spark>. In real mode this is [] for the 112 non-enriched ASINs and a single value for the 8 enriched. The dashboard/bestsellers/movers all render these rows. Spark (a fixed-size LineChart) draws nothing for [] and no line for 1 point; the good/bad color is computed from first==last==0.
findings.evidence: rank-row.tsx:13 `const hist = getBsrHistory(p.asin).points.map(pt=>pt.value);` with no length check; line 39 `<Spark data={hist} invert/>`. SSR-probe confirmed Spark with data=[] and data=[1pt] both render without throwing. The spark wrapper is aria-hidden (line 38), so screen-reader impact is nil, but visually the lg sparkline column is blank for ~93% of rows.
findings.impact: Empty sparkline cells across the main list screens (lg breakpoint). Cosmetic/quality, not a crash, and a11y-neutral because the element is aria-hidden.
findings.fix: In RankRow, only render <Spark> when hist.filter(v=>v!=null).length >= 2; otherwise render a muted '—' or omit the column. Avoids drawing empty charts and the meaningless first/last color heuristic on a single point.

findings.area: Locale toggle flips RTL direction but does not translate the UI
findings.issue: LocaleToggle sets document.documentElement.dir='rtl' and lang='ar' on click, but every chrome string is rendered from labelEn/nameEn/English literals (sidebar groups, nav items, page titles, KPI labels, disclosures). Toggling to Arabic mirrors the entire layout to RTL while all surrounding text stays English — producing a mixed-direction, broken-looking layout (English right-aligned, sidebar mirrored, lucide icons flipped to the wrong side) with no real Arabic translation.
findings.evidence: top-bar.tsx:24-25 sets dir/lang only; no i18n state propagates. app-sidebar.tsx renders {group.labelEn} (line 69) and {item.labelEn} (86) regardless of locale; constants.ts holds labelAr/nameAr but they are unused by the shell. page-header.tsx renders the passed English `title` verbatim. The real titleAr Arabic product names ARE correctly marked dir="rtl" font-arabic inline (verified in rank-row, product-card, watch-card, detail page) — that part is good.
findings.impact: The toggle advertises a bilingual product but only mirrors direction; switching to Arabic degrades rather than localizes the UI. Confusing for the target (Egyptian) audience; an a11y/i18n correctness gap since lang='ar' is set on an all-English document.
findings.fix: Either (a) gate the toggle to a real i18n layer that swaps labelEn↔labelAr (the Arabic strings already exist in constants), or (b) until that exists, scope dir changes to genuinely bilingual blocks and keep the document LTR, or remove the global dir flip so lang/dir never contradict the rendered content.

findings.area: Demand-band inconsistency between search/watch cards (absolute BSR) and list/store (within-category)
findings.issue: Search and watch cards compute the demand band from ABSOLUTE BSR thresholds (bsr<300 very-high, <1000 high, <3000 moderate). On real data, product.bsr is leaf?.rank ?? row.rank — for the 8 enriched products it is the leaf-category rank (often 1-2 in a narrow leaf like 'USB Cables'), and for others it is the 1-120 bestseller position. Neither matches the within-category percentile band (bandFromPos) used by the lists/store, so the same product can show a different band on search vs bestsellers.
findings.evidence: search product-card.tsx:17-21 absolute thresholds; real-store.ts rowToProduct line 104 `bsr: leaf?.rank ?? row.rank`; bandFromPos (66-73) uses positional fraction within category. types.ts:69-73 explicitly documents the band as 'within a category … Never comparable across categories', which the absolute-threshold helpers violate.
findings.impact: Cross-screen band labels can disagree for the same ASIN; contradicts the documented within-category semantics. Lower severity because search results derive from the seed/real catalogue and the discrepancy is bounded, but it undermines the 'one source of truth' intent noted in data.ts:121.
findings.fix: Have search/watch cards consume the band from the data layer (carry demandBand on the Product or look it up via the bestseller row) instead of recomputing from absolute BSR. Delete the duplicated demandBandFromBsr helpers.

findings.area: Alerts link to seed-only product pages
findings.issue: getAlerts() seeds three alerts on the same seed ASINs (B0EG0XIAM2/PHIL6/LORE9). The alerts table itself renders fine (it uses alert.productTitle, a literal string, so no crash), but each row links to /products/{seedAsin}. Those ASINs exist in bestsellers.all? No — they are seed-only, so getProduct→real.product returns undefined and the detail route calls notFound() → 404.
findings.evidence: data.ts:362-392 hardcodes the seed ASINs; alerts/page.tsx:123 `href={`/products/${alert.asin}`}`. Detail page page.tsx:97 `if (!product) notFound();`. Confirmed the three ASINs are absent from real data (same probe as the Critical finding).
findings.impact: Clicking any seeded alert's product link 404s. Dead links from a populated table; no crash on the alerts page itself.
findings.fix: Seed alerts from real ASINs (e.g. the top few getBestSellers() rows) so productTitle and the link target are consistent and resolvable, or hide the link when the ASIN is not tracked.

dimensions.summary: The migration is syntactically valid Postgres/Supabase DDL and the core time-series model (append-only `snapshots`/`rankings` + supporting indexes) is sound and WOULD support getBsrHistory and derived movers if wired. The `riser_daily` view's window logic is actually correct (the explicit full-partition frame defends against the classic last_value pitfall, DESC ordering gives now/prev correctly, and the Δlog(BSR) sign matches types.ts). However there is one Critical RLS gap: `watchlist_items` is never RLS-enabled and has no policy, so once auth is on it leaks/accepts cross-tenant rows. A second structural defect: per-ASIN leaf BSR is stored as a display name in `rankings.bsr_category` (text), which cannot join to `categories.node_id`, so the riser_daily/demand-band "leaf rank" key the spec relies on is not actually keyed to the category tree. The overarching context — which caps the verdict — is that the ENTIRE schema is currently unwired dead code: the running app reads JSON files (web/src/data/real/*.json) via real-store.ts, there is no Supabase/pg client or dependency anywhere in web/, and the scrapers write JSON, not the DB. So none of this SQL is exercised in the current runtime; it is a forward-looking spec (DEPLOY.md "Option B").

findings.area: RLS / tenant isolation
findings.issue: watchlist_items has NO row-level security enabled and NO policy, while its parent watchlists is RLS-isolated. RLS is enabled only on watchlists, alerts (lines 165-167); watchlist_items is omitted.
findings.evidence: Lines 165-167 enable RLS on watchlists/watchlist_items/alerts — but line 166 IS present for watchlist_items, yet there is NO `create policy` for watchlist_items (only tenant_rw_watchlists line 169 and tenant_rw_alerts line 172). In Postgres, enabling RLS with zero policies = DENY ALL to non-owners, which actually BREAKS the feature: the anon/authenticated app role can read/write watchlists (policy exists) but every join/select to watchlist_items returns zero rows and every insert is rejected, because no policy grants access. watchlist_items also has no tenant_id column (line 145-150), so a correct policy must filter via EXISTS on the parent watchlist — which is not written.
findings.impact: Watchlist contents are entirely inaccessible through the anon/authenticated role once auth+RLS is on (feature silently returns empty), OR if a developer 'fixes' it by simply disabling RLS on the child, items become globally readable across tenants — a data-isolation breach for a multi-tenant SaaS. Either way the tenant model is broken for the items table.
findings.fix: Add a policy that scopes items through their parent watchlist, e.g.: `create policy tenant_rw_watchlist_items on watchlist_items using (exists (select 1 from watchlists w where w.id = watchlist_id and w.tenant_id = (auth.jwt()->>'tenant_id')::uuid)) with check (same)`. Apply the identical EXISTS-on-parent pattern. Do the same review for any future child tables.

findings.area: Schema-vs-app key integrity (leaf BSR ↔ category tree)
findings.issue: The leaf-category key that the demand-band / riser logic depends on is stored as a free-text display NAME, not as a categories.node_id FK, so leaf rankings cannot be joined to the category tree.
findings.evidence: parse.py:127 emits `{'rank': int, 'category': cat.strip()}` where cat is the human label ('USB Cables', 'Electronics') scraped from the BSR table. The migration's rankings.category_node (line 80) is `not null references categories(node_id)` — but the spec (04-real-pipeline-spec.md §2.3/§2.7) says the meaningful leaf key is the harvested numeric node-id (e.g. 21833243031), captured from the `<a href>` , NOT the label. The migration provides bsr_category text (line 84) for the label but there is no FK column for the leaf node-id, and category_node is forced to the LIST category (e.g. 'electronics'), not the leaf. So 'leaf rank' (#5 in USB Cables) cannot resolve to a categories row, and riser_daily partitions by (asin, category_node) = the LIST node, mixing list-rank-derived bsr with leaf bsr.
findings.impact: riser_daily and the within-category demand band cannot actually operate on the leaf category the spec claims is 'the meaningful key'. Cross-category BSR values (whole-Electronics rank vs USB-Cables leaf rank) can be co-mingled under one category_node, producing an incorrect/misleading Δlog(BSR) — the exact cross-category comparison the app's C1 control forbids.
findings.fix: Add `bsr_leaf_node text references categories(node_id)` and persist the harvested numeric node-id from parse.py (extend parse to capture the leaf node-id from `tr td a[href*="/gp/bestsellers/"]` as §2.3 specifies). Partition riser_daily by the leaf node, and backfill categories with the numeric sub-nodes (§2.7) before relying on the FK.

findings.area: Dead/unwired data model (architecture correctness)
findings.location: supabase/migrations/0001_init.sql (whole file) vs web/src (no client) and scrapers/run.py:98-116
findings.issue: The entire SQL schema is not connected to anything in the running system: the app reads JSON files, not Postgres, and the scraper writes JSON files, not the DB.
findings.evidence: (1) No DB client or dependency: grep for supabase/@supabase/pg/postgres/drizzle/prisma/kysely across web/src and web/package.json returns nothing. (2) The app's data seam reads files: real-store.ts:10 `import {readFileSync} from 'node:fs'`, :25 `DIR = .../src/data/real`, and data.ts delegates to it (e.g. data.ts:67 `if (real.available()) return real.bsrHistory(asin)`). (3) The scraper writes JSON only: run.py:98-116 writes bestsellers.json/products.json/meta.json; grep for INSERT/upsert/supabase in scrapers/*.py finds none. (4) .env.example:6-10 leaves all SUPABASE_* blank and states 'NOTHING here is required for the current local file-store model'. DEPLOY.md:46-55 frames Supabase as a future 'Option B'.
findings.impact: Every SQL-correctness property (FKs, indexes, RLS, riser_daily) is currently inert — it protects/serves no live traffic. getBsrHistory in the live path returns a single point (real-store.ts:167-177) because there is no append-only history table feeding it; the migration's claim that snapshots 'make BSR history real over time' is not realized. Risk: schema drift — the JSON shapes (run.py) and the DDL can diverge silently since nothing enforces them together (and they already differ: JSON has no snapshots/append concept).
findings.fix: Either (a) clearly mark the migration as a not-yet-wired spec and add a CI check that the scraper's JSON contract matches the intended row schema, or (b) implement the documented upsert step (write products/snapshots/rankings/reviews/keyword_snapshots) and the SupabaseReadAdapter so the schema is actually exercised before its correctness can be trusted.

findings.area: View semantics (riser_daily window / lag definition)
findings.issue: rise_score uses last_value over an 8-day window = the OLDEST snapshot still inside the window as 'prev', not a fixed lag (e.g. yesterday or 7d ago). The reference window therefore drifts with snapshot density and age.
findings.evidence: Lines 183-185: `where captured_at > now() - interval '8 days'` with frame `rows between unbounded preceding and unbounded following` order by captured_at desc. bsr_prev = last_value = oldest row in the 8d window. There is no day-bucketing despite the view name 'riser_daily'; two products with different snapshot histories are compared over different effective intervals (one over ~1 day, one over ~8 days). The app's own riseScore (data.ts:106-113) instead uses a fixed window index (period 2/7/30), so server view and client logic compute DIFFERENT deltas.
findings.impact: rise_score is not a per-day or per-7-day velocity; it is 'change since the oldest point in the last 8 days', which over- or under-states movers depending on cadence and how long an item has been tracked. Ranking of movers is inconsistent and not comparable across products; it also diverges from the client-side getMovers definition, so a Supabase-backed movers list would not match the seed-backed one.
findings.fix: Define the lag explicitly: pick bsr_prev as the snapshot closest to now()-interval '7 days' (or '1 day') per (asin, leaf node) using a lateral/ordered subquery or date_trunc('day') bucketing, and document the exact window so it matches data.ts riseScore. Optionally add a min-2-snapshots guard so single-snapshot ASINs are excluded rather than yielding rise_score=0.

findings.area: Missing index / query performance
findings.issue: Key read paths lack supporting indexes. (1) reviews has only reviews_asin (line 120) but no index on review_sentiment.review_id beyond its PK (ok), however reviews has no index for 'newest reviews' ordering; more importantly (2) rankings has no index on (list_type) or (category_node, list_type, captured_at) for the very common 'newest bestsellers in category' query, and snapshots/rankings 'latest row per asin' has no covering DISTINCT ON support.
findings.evidence: Indexes present: snapshots_asin_time (75), snapshots_time_brin (76), rankings_cat_time (90), rankings_asin_time (91), products_brand_idx (61), products_cat_idx (62), reviews_asin (120). The dominant app query (real-store.ts:128-134 bestSellers, spec §5.4 'newest rankings rows where list_type=bestsellers, filter category, order by rank') filters by list_type and category_node and wants the latest captured_at — rankings_cat_time covers (category_node, captured_at) but not list_type, so list_type is a post-filter, and there is no index to fetch list_rank ordering directly.
findings.impact: At scale (append-only table grows unbounded), 'latest bestsellers per category' does an index range scan plus filter+sort; acceptable early but degrades as snapshots accumulate (the whole point of append-only). Not Critical because volumes are tiny today and nothing queries it yet.
findings.fix: Add `create index rankings_cat_list_time on rankings (category_node, list_type, captured_at desc)` and consider a partial index `where list_type='bestsellers'`. For 'latest snapshot per asin', rely on the existing snapshots_asin_time (already DESC) with DISTINCT ON (asin) — verify the planner uses it.

findings.area: Source-id referential consistency (keywords)
findings.issue: keyword_snapshots.source defaults to 'google_trends' and is not a FK, while the actual pipeline labels the source 'amazon_eg_autocomplete (completion.amazon.co.uk) + google_trends' and the app emits source 'amazon_autocomplete' — none of which is constrained, so source strings are free-form and inconsistent across layers.
findings.evidence: Migration line 104 `source text not null default 'google_trends'` (no FK to sources). sources seed (193-198) defines ids amazon_html_bestsellers/_product/_reviews/google_trends — NOT 'amazon_autocomplete' or 'amazon_eg_autocomplete'. data.ts:299 emits provenance source 'amazon_autocomplete'; keywords.json 'source' = 'amazon_eg_autocomplete (completion.amazon.co.uk) + google_trends'. snapshots.source (line 68) and rankings.source (87) ARE FK-constrained to sources(id), but the app/scraper would need to insert 'amazon_html_bestsellers' to satisfy them — not yet exercised.
findings.impact: Low today (table unused), but once wired, keyword provenance is unconstrained free text and will not reconcile with the sources catalogue, and any attempt to insert snapshot/ranking rows with the app's provenance strings (e.g. 'amazon_autocomplete') would violate the sources FK. Minor data-quality / join-consistency risk.
findings.fix: Either FK keyword_snapshots.source to sources(id) and register the autocomplete/google_trends source ids the pipeline actually uses, or document source as a free label. Align the source-id vocabulary across parse/run, data.ts provenance, and the sources seed.

findings.area: Constraint completeness / data hygiene
findings.issue: Several columns that should be bounded/non-null are unconstrained: scrape_runs.status and snapshots.confidence are free text with no CHECK; numeric fields (price_egp, rating, demand_score, null_rate, gain_pct) have no range checks; rating could be any number.
findings.evidence: Line 37 status text (comment 'ok|partial|failed|blocked' not enforced); line 72 confidence text (comment 'high|medium|low' not enforced, unlike the app's Confidence union type in types.ts:14); line 69 price_egp numeric, line 70 rating numeric (no 0–5 CHECK), line 102 demand_score numeric (comment '0–100' not enforced), line 39 null_rate numeric (0–1 not enforced).
findings.impact: Garbage values (negative price, rating 7.0, demand_score 250) can be stored and then surfaced by the UI as facts; the DB provides no backstop for the scraper's parse errors. The app's TS unions (Confidence/DemandBand) are stricter than the DB, so the DB is the weaker contract.
findings.fix: Add CHECK constraints: rating between 0 and 5; price_egp >= 0; demand_score between 0 and 100; null_rate between 0 and 1; status in ('ok','partial','failed','blocked'); confidence in ('high','medium','low'). Mirror the TS unions in the DDL.

verified: Postgres syntax is valid: gen_random_uuid() default (0001_init.sql:8,139,152), `bigint generated always as identity` (33,95,130), `using brin (captured_at)` (76), window functions with named WINDOW clause (184-185), ln()/nullif() (188), auth.jwt()->>'tenant_id' cast to uuid (170-171), `on conflict (id) do nothing` (198), composite PKs (73,88,106,149) — all parse as valid Postgres/Supabase DDL; no syntax errors found.

PK/FK wiring is internally consistent: products.asin PK (52) referenced by snapshots/rankings/reviews/watchlist_items/alerts; categories.node_id PK (44) self-references parent_node (47) and is referenced by products/rankings; tenants/app_users/watchlists/alerts tenancy chain is coherent with ON DELETE CASCADE on tenant_id (16,142,153).

Append-only design is structurally correct for history: snapshots PK (asin, captured_at, source) (73) and rankings PK (asin, category_node, captured_at, source) (88) permit one row per capture without overwriting, and snapshots_asin_time / rankings_asin_time DESC indexes (75,91) support 'history for one ASIN' and 'latest per ASIN' — so getBsrHistory and derived movers ARE supportable by the schema in principle.

riser_daily window logic is CORRECT (not the suspected bug): the explicit frame `rows between unbounded preceding and unbounded following` (185) makes last_value scan the full partition (avoiding the classic last_value default-frame pitfall); with `order by captured_at desc`, first_value=newest=bsr_now and last_value=oldest=bsr_prev; rise_score = ln(bsr_prev) - ln(bsr_now) (188) is positive when rank improved, matching types.ts:84 'ln(bsrPrev) - ln(bsrNow). Positive = improving'. nullif(...,0) guards ln(0)/divide; the where clause (190) drops null endpoints.

RLS USING + WITH CHECK are both present and correct for the two policied tables: tenant_rw_watchlists (169-171) and tenant_rw_alerts (172-174) each filter both read (using) and write (with check) by tenant_id = jwt tenant_id, correctly preventing cross-tenant read and cross-tenant insert/update for those two tables.

Schema column set broadly matches the app's domain types: products/snapshots/rankings/reviews/keywords cover Product/SeriesPoint/RankingRow/Review/Keyword fields in types.ts; is_estimated + confidence columns (71-72,103-105) back the Provenance.isEstimated/confidence discipline the UI relies on.
